claims.text: Optimizing Al and Cr content promotes formation of a thin, adherent, continuous mixed Al2O3/Cr2O3 surface scale.
The mixed Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The mixed Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale enhances corrosion behavior.
Formation of the mixed oxide scale permits retention of mechanical strength.
A cast Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy with suboptimal Al and Cr levels forms a minimal or discontinuous oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
Increasing the proportions of Al and Cr favors selective and spontaneous formation of a robust passivating scale during thermal exposure.
Increased Al and Cr content drives selective oxidation at elevated temperature.
A continuous Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale acts as a barrier to ingress of oxygen and corrosive species.
The protective surface layer does not affect the underlying bulk composition responsible for mechanical strength and low density.
At 800 degrees Celsius in air for 100 hours, the compositionally tuned alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the baseline alloy.
The compositionally tuned alloy will show less oxide-scale spallation than the baseline alloy.
The compositionally tuned alloy will develop fewer and shallower corrosion pits in cyclic salt-spray testing than the baseline alloy.
The compositionally tuned alloy will maintain mechanical strength comparable to the baseline alloy.
Failure to form a continuous, adherent oxide scale will eliminate the predicted improvements in environmental resistance.
The lower-Al/Cr baseline has moderate oxidation and corrosion resistance without compromised mechanical properties.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate near 800 degrees Celsius for exposure times of approximately 100 hours.
The mechanism may cease to hold above 1000 degrees Celsius or under more aggressive thermal cycling because of scale spallation or oxide-phase instability.
